# Neutral tiny consumer contract for independent review

This is a new isolated experimental consumer, not production training code. Review ONLY the explicit symmetric LNC2 feature-ownership change from d0f0d7fb consumer4939265b to the candidate source whose hashes accompany this packet.

Shape V256/C128/T256; FP32 or BF16 input gradient, FP32 output. Metadata counts/starts/positions/group maxima is supplied by fixed synthetic fixtures, not built on device or timed. Stable per-row token positions are required. Each output element starts at positive zero and receives one FP32 addition for each occurrence in original token order. Inactive rows retain their prior bits. No cross-tile sums, reassociation, tolerance, routing or data change.

Expected ownership: two programs via explicit grid[2]. Both visit groups0/1 and use the same dynamic bound for each group, including unequal group maxima. Program0 columns0:64, program1 columns64:128. Every output element must have one writer. The program index must not alter branches, row groups, loop counts, metadata or token ordering.

Reference14572563 and checker89189024 are unchanged full files. Checker remains default-disabled; native opt-in requires four ranks and LNC2. Existing20 native cases/150 comparisons per rank are strict full-output bytes, including signed zero and subnormals; all four receipts must complete. Nonfinite metrics stay serializable and cannot count as exactness. No native acceptance follows from compilation alone.

Original raw rank0 failure and compiler log are included without interpretation. Ranks1–3 terminal receipts were absent after torchrun termination; do not invent them. Old route remains parked. Actual old cache key includes [1]; cause of the compiler failure remains to be determined. Independent review should assess documented NKI0.5 support, actual changed source, output ownership, runtime-flow symmetry, offset semantics and CPU reference behavior. No host execution or adoption is requested.

## Fresh independent-session constraints

You receive only the full-context source diff, this neutral contract and original raw gate receipts. No repository, prior session, implementation notes or prior reviewer conclusions are available. Do not use network, AWS, hosts, credentials, external data or weights. Do not start native or model training. Default REFUSE until the evidence needed for this limited source/CPU gate is complete. Reconstruct the exact candidate from the diff and independently write and RUN at least one tiny CPU reference test of an exactness claim: ordered FP32 accumulation, exact feature ownership or symmetric per-program control schedules. Use stdlib and tiny synthetic inputs; no SDK/model import, large allocations or installation. CPU emulation cannot prove NKI lowering, native roundoff, speed or full training. Do not call a native compiler result proved by source. Return REPORT.md plus your independently written test and raw outputs in /work; explicitly identify limits and any precise blocking defect. No code edits to the candidate.

    13	    import nki.isa as nisa
    14	    import nki.language as nl

    16	    @nki.jit
    17	    def resident_consumer(gradient, counts, starts, positions, group_maximums):

    20	        assert gradient.shape == (256, 128)

    24	        assert counts.dtype == starts.dtype == positions.dtype == group_maximums.dtype == nl.int32
    25	        assert nl.num_programs() == 2
    26	        feature_first = nl.program_id(0) * 64
    27	        output = nl.ndarray((256, 128), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    28	        for group in range(2):
    29	            first = group * 128
    30	            remaining = nl.ndarray((128, 1), dtype=nl.int32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    31	            pointer = nl.ndarray((128, 1), dtype=nl.int32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    32	            nisa.dma_copy(dst=remaining, src=counts[first:first + 128, :])
    33	            nisa.dma_copy(dst=pointer, src=starts[first:first + 128, :])
    34	            maximum = nl.ndarray((1, 1), dtype=nl.int32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    35	            nisa.dma_copy(dst=maximum, src=group_maximums[group:group + 1, :])
    36	            limit = nisa.register_alloc(0)
    37	            nisa.register_load(limit, maximum)
    38	            accumulator = nl.full((128, 64), 0.0, dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    39	            sentinel = nl.full((128, 1), 256, dtype=nl.int32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    40	            active = nl.ndarray((128, 1), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    41	            updated = nl.ndarray((128, 64), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    42	            for _ in nl.dynamic_range(limit):
    43	                nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=active, data=remaining, op0=nl.greater, operand0=0.0,
    44	                                   engine=nisa.engine.vector)
    45	                address = nl.where(active, pointer, sentinel, dtype=nl.int32)
    46	                # Skipped lanes retain a valid initialized sentinel, never stale
    47	                # prior-iteration addresses. Both indirect reads skip inactive rows.
    48	                token = nl.full((128, 1), 256, dtype=nl.int32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    49	                nisa.dma_copy(dst=token,
    50	                              src=positions.ap(pattern=[[1, 128], [1, 1]],
    51	                                               vector_offset=address, indirect_dim=0),
    52	                              oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip, dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.swdge)
    53	                token_address = nl.where(active, token, sentinel, dtype=nl.int32)
    54	                value = nl.full((128, 64), 0.0, dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    55	                nisa.dma_copy(dst=value,
    56	                              src=gradient.ap(pattern=[[128, 128], [1, 64]], offset=feature_first,
    57	                                              vector_offset=token_address, indirect_dim=0),
    58	                              oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip, dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.swdge)
    59	                # Exactly one FP32 addition per occurrence, no gradient reduction
    60	                # or tree/segment sum. Preserve inactive accumulator bits by select.
    61	                nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=updated, data1=accumulator, data2=value,
    62	                                   op=nl.add, engine=nisa.engine.vector)
    63	                selected = nl.where(active.ap(pattern=[[1, 128], [0, 64]]),
    64	                                    updated, accumulator, dtype=nl.float32)
    65	                nisa.tensor_copy(dst=accumulator, src=selected)

    67	                                   engine=nisa.engine.vector)
    68	                nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=remaining, data=remaining, op0=nl.add, operand0=-1.0,
    69	                                   engine=nisa.engine.vector)
    70	            # Both programs visit every row group with identical runtime limits.
    71	            # Each writes only its own feature half, including positive-zero unused rows.
    72	            nisa.dma_copy(dst=output[first:first + 128, feature_first:feature_first + 64], src=accumulator)
